source_identity.title: Ransomware Execution PROvenance Dataset (REPROD)
source_identity.resource_type_caution: Zenodo and DataCite classify the record as a conference paper even though the record exposes dataset artifacts. This is a metadata-quality warning and does not by itself invalidate immutable artifact identity.

official_execution_and_lineage_declarati.raw_pml_filename_semantics: The official description states that PML files are named using the MalwareBazaar SHA-256 of the executed ransomware binary.
official_execution_and_lineage_declarati.source_native_group_key_candidate: MalwareBazaar SHA-256 associated with a PML execution
official_execution_and_lineage_declarati.dot_outputs_lineage_rule: Every DOT output is a derived SPADE/query view and must remain grouped with its originating PML execution.

associated_publication_verification.venue: 2023 Cyber Security Experimentation and Test Workshop
associated_publication_verification.scientific_implication: The publication and formal dataset citation verify the provenance of the research artifact, but they do not close source-native execution grouping, reset, duplicate-run, pointer, or split-independence requirements.

workflow_repository_metadata.implication: No REPROD workflow code is approved for use. A future PML reader and SPADE transformation must be separately identified, version-pinned, hash-pinned, and reviewed before any content audit.

evidence_fit.class_balance_implication: All declared executions are ransomware; this family cannot by itself provide benign or null training capacity.

label_supervision_and_pointer_isolation.candidate_pointer_shape: record DOI + artifact key + opaque execution SHA-256 + member identity + event or graph-record index

evidence: Zenodo revision 2 and DataCite agree on DOI, concept DOI, title, creator set, version 1.0, open access, and CC-BY-4.0 rights.
Zenodo publishes 15 objects totaling 144708035023 bytes and an MD5 for every object.
The official description declares 405 PML executions named by the MalwareBazaar SHA-256 of the executed ransomware binary and 861 DOT outputs derived from those executions.
Crossref verifies the matching-author ACM CSET 2023 paper and its reference to the REPROD concept DOI.
Official metadata does not publish an immutable execution manifest, a VM reset or snapshot contract, a duplicate-run policy, or a verified PML-to-DOT binding.
The workflow repository has no release, tag, or declared repository license, and no repository content was read.
inference: REPROD satisfies the metadata threshold for a separately reviewable executed-evidence candidate because the execution count and SHA-256 grouping semantics are curator-declared rather than inferred from file counts or class paths.
The 861 DOT files are derived views and cannot increase lineage count beyond their originating PML executions.

Opaque SHA-256 identifiers are plausible split-group keys, but they cannot receive lineage credit until a bounded manifest audit proves unique, non-duplicate execution membership and preserves all derived views in the same split.
The source has strong endpoint and provenance relevance but no benign or null capacity and therefore cannot independently repair training class balance.
The record-level CC-BY-4.0 license permits metadata candidacy, while nested notices, third-party terms, and reader/tool identity remain training blockers.
recommendation: Approve REPROD only as a metadata candidate; do not assign a train role, family credit, lineage credit, sample credit, quota, or catalog entry.
If separately authorized, first freeze an exact bounded acquisition contract. The current review does not choose between the 124.59 GiB raw multipart and the 10.18 GiB derived archive.
Require central-directory and nested-notice inspection before any member-content, schema, pointer, manifest, duplicate-run, reset, or PML-to-DOT audit.
Keep summary.csv and all family, detector, verdict, answer, and ground-truth surfaces physically outside model-visible input, targets, pointers, and grouping decisions.
Fail closed if at least four unique executions, stable pointer surfaces, protected exclusion, or rights isolation cannot be verified without labels or hidden ground truth.

future_bounded_audit_requirements: Pin one exact artifact choice or an explicitly bounded multipart subset, record revision, object keys, byte sizes, MD5 values, canonical content URLs, byte ceiling, resume policy, and retry ceiling before acquisition.
Identify and hash-pin the PML central-directory reader before any raw multipart inspection; identify and hash-pin any DOT reader separately.
Inspect central-directory metadata and nested license or notice material before reading member content.
Prove that at least four unique SHA-256 identifiers map to distinct non-empty PML executions without using summary.csv, malware-family labels, detector outputs, or hidden ground truth.
Determine whether repeated executions or duplicate SHA-256 members exist and keep every repeat and every derived DOT view in the same lineage and split.
Audit or retain as unverified the VM reset, snapshot restore, and sandbox reinitialization contract between executions.
Pin the SPADE transformation identity and verify the PML-to-DOT mapping before treating DOT records as evidence derived from a specific execution.
Freeze a field-level allowlist and prove record pointer recoverability for the chosen evidence surface.
Run protected exact and near-duplicate exclusion before any sample, role, lineage, or quota decision.
